existing_structural_draft.name: SQLite
existing_structural_draft.summary: A serverless embedded relational engine that compiles SQL into bytecode, executes it in a virtual machine, and persists database state through a layered B-tree, pager, journaling, and VFS design.

features.name: Embedded process execution
features.description: SQLite is designed as a local database engine linked into an application rather than as a separately managed client/server process. Its primary target is local application and device storage, although it can also serve as an application-specific server-side storage engine.
benefits: Avoids a separately deployed database daemon
Keeps the engine close to the application and its data
Works in environments with limited administration or unreliable connectivity
costs: Database lifecycle and resource use are coupled to the host process
Direct multi-host network access is a poor fit
High concurrent write workloads may require a client/server database

features.name: SQL compilation to bytecode and virtual-machine execution
features.description: SQLite compiles SQL text into bytecode stored in a prepared statement and executes that program with a virtual machine. Tokenization, parsing, code generation, and bytecode execution are distinct stages.
benefits: Separates declarative SQL input from execution machinery
Provides a compact intermediate execution representation
Creates a stable boundary for query-planning and execution logic
costs: Adds compilation and intermediate-representation machinery
The bytecode model is an implementation-specific execution contract

features.name: Layered B-tree and pager storage
features.description: Tables and indexes are represented by B-trees stored in a database file. The pager mediates fixed-size page I/O, caching, locking, rollback, and commit behavior between the B-tree layer and the operating-system interface.
benefits: Provides indexed relational storage over fixed-size pages
Centralizes caching and durability coordination in the pager
Allows higher layers to depend on an abstract page interface
costs: Page-level coordination and caching add implementation complexity
Performance depends on filesystem, device, and cache behavior

features.name: Journal-based atomic commit and recovery
features.description: In rollback-journal mode, SQLite records original pages before modifying the database and uses the journal to restore an interrupted transaction. The presence and validity of a hot journal determine whether recovery is required after a crash.
benefits: Provides atomic transaction behavior across crashes and power loss under documented assumptions
Makes recovery automatic to the application
Supports multi-file atomic commit through a super-journal design
costs: Journal writes and synchronization increase commit I/O
Correctness depends on operating-system and filesystem assumptions
Recovery and locking introduce additional state transitions

features.name: Write-ahead logging with reader snapshots
features.description: In WAL mode, committed changes are appended to a separate log and readers use an end mark to observe a stable database snapshot while a writer appends. Checkpointing later transfers WAL content back into the main database file.
benefits: Allows readers and a writer to make progress concurrently in common cases
Turns many writes into sequential log appends
Provides a snapshot-like read boundary for each reader transaction
costs: There is still only one writer for a database file
Long-running readers can delay checkpoint completion
WAL requires same-host shared-memory coordination and creates sidecar files

features.name: Virtual file system portability boundary
features.description: SQLite communicates with the operating system through a VFS abstraction that supplies file, time, randomness, locking, and related platform operations. Unix and Windows implementations provide concrete VFSes, and custom VFS implementations can be registered.
benefits: Separates database mechanisms from platform-specific file behavior
Supports portability across operating systems
Allows specialized deployments to adapt filesystem capabilities
costs: The abstraction must accurately expose filesystem and device properties
Incorrect or unusual filesystem behavior can invalidate durability assumptions

mathematical_views.model: Relational algebra to bytecode operational semantics
mathematical_views.question: How can declarative SQL be transformed into an executable program while preserving the intended query result?
assumptions: SQL statements can be represented by a relational or procedural execution plan
The compiler and virtual machine agree on the bytecode instruction semantics
This view abstracts away optimizer cost-model details

mathematical_views.question: Which transaction states and recovery transitions preserve the appearance of atomic commit?
assumptions: The operating system provides the file and synchronization behavior assumed by SQLite
Journal metadata and page records are modeled as durable state transitions
The model distinguishes rollback-journal mode from WAL mode

mathematical_views.question: Which storage and operating-system details can be changed behind the B-tree and pager interfaces without changing the SQL-facing contract?
assumptions: The VFS implementation satisfies the behavioral assumptions required by the pager
The observation concerns interface behavior rather than performance equivalence
Custom VFSes are evaluated against the relevant durability and locking contract

benefits: Low deployment and IPC overhead
Good fit for local and device-resident data
costs: Weak fit for many clients writing through a shared network service
Less process isolation than a separately deployed database

benefits: Composable execution pipeline
Reusable prepared statement representation
costs: Requires compiler, bytecode, and VM maintenance

benefits: Clear separation between logical storage and page/device mechanics
costs: Cross-layer invariants are required for correctness

benefits: Crash recovery and atomic transaction semantics
costs: Additional writes, synchronization, locks, and recovery work

benefits: Reader/writer overlap and sequential append behavior
costs: Checkpoint coordination, sidecar files, and same-host constraints

benefits: Portability and specialized filesystem integration
costs: More assumptions must be expressed and validated at the platform boundary

modeling_task.objective: Transform repository evidence into a reviewed-quality, evidence-backed architecture model.
questions: What are the system's core abstractions and state components?
Which operations change state, and what invariants do they preserve?
Which reusable architecture features are supported by evidence?
Which mathematical views explain those features, under which assumptions?
What benefits, costs, failure modes, and counterexamples apply?
evidence_rules: Do not promote a path name or file count into a semantic fact.
Every feature and mathematical view must cite evidence IDs.
Use hypothesis or analogy when the mathematical correspondence is not established.
Keep product-specific facts separate from transferable feature names.
